stem: Problem 1.1 The lifetimes (in hours) of computer chips produced by a certain semiconductor firm are exponentially distributed with parameter \(\lambda\). Suppose that the prior distribution on \(\lambda\) is the Gamma distribution with parameters \((3,1)\). If the average life of the first \(20\) chips tested is \(4.6\) hours, find posterior density \(\pi(\lambda \mid \mathbf x)\) and identify it. Hint: this is another Gamma distribution

solution.reason: For 20 exponential observations, the likelihood is proportional to λ^20 exp(-λΣxᵢ). Since Σxᵢ=20·4.6=92, combining it with the Gamma(3,1) prior gives Gamma(3+20,1+92)=Gamma(23,93).

stem: Problem 1.2 The lifetimes (in hours) of computer chips produced by a certain semiconductor firm are exponentially distributed with parameter 𝜆. Suppose that the prior distribution on 𝜆 is the Gamma distribution with parameters (3,1). If the average life of the first 20 chips tested is 4.6 hours, find the Bayes estimate of 𝜆.

solution.reason: The posterior is Gamma(23,93). Under the default quadratic loss, the Bayes estimate is its posterior mean, 23/93.

stem: Problem 2.3 Find confidence level of confidence interval [ ―― 𝐱 −𝜎/√𝑛, ―― 𝐱 +𝜎/√𝑛] for the mean 𝜇 and a sample 𝐱 of size 𝑛 from a normal distribution with standard deviation 𝜎. Several values of the c.d.f. Φ of a standard normal distribution are Φ⁡(1) =0.841, Φ⁡(2) =0.977, Φ⁡(3) =0.999.

solution.reason: Since √n(x̄−μ)/σ is standard normal, the confidence level is P(|Z|≤1)=2Φ(1)−1=2(0.841)−1=0.682.
